subject.title: Policy plugins cannot see resolved/served model identity at any blocking-capable hook (security impact: our confidentiality guard failed open)

question: Should OpenClaw expose selected provider/model identity through the existing `before_agent_run` hook context/event, or add a separate post-resolve pre-call hook/provider attribution contract?
rationale: This is both a plugin SDK contract and a confidentiality enforcement boundary; source shows a narrow runner inconsistency, but the issue also asks for broader served-model and provider-hook semantics.

options.title: Extend the existing gate consistently
options.body: Add read-only provider/model fields to the existing blocking hook contract across all runner paths, with docs and focused plugin tests, while tracking actual proxy backend identity separately.

options.title: Add a new pre-call hook
options.body: Introduce a post-resolve/pre-provider hook for policy enforcement, accepting the larger API/security review cost of a new public hook surface.

options.title: Limit this to audit telemetry
options.body: Keep blocking hooks unchanged and only document `model_call_*` audit metadata, leaving confidentiality enforcement to config-derived agent eligibility workarounds.

recommendation.title: Extend the existing gate consistently
recommendation.body: Add read-only provider/model fields to the existing blocking hook contract across all runner paths, with docs and focused plugin tests, while tracking actual proxy backend identity separately.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent hook and CLI-context history makes this the best available routing candidate for the contract choice, with `jesse-merhi` as the original gate-history reference.
